name: ESP32 DevKitC, 38 pins (clone)
description: ESP32 development board: ESP-WROOM-32 module, CP2102 USB-to-serial, micro-USB, 3.3 V regulator, RST and BOOT buttons. Pin order equal to Espressif's ESP32-DevKitC V4.

identified.how: from the owner's photo (photos/top.jpg): module marking ESP-WROOM-32, chip marking CP2102, the printed pin labels; the owner confirmed the left side's labels

mounting: through-hole: two rows of 19 male header pins

row_spacing.source: the owner, 2026-11-19; the top photo, scaled by the pitch, agrees

board.source: Espressif's DevKitC V4 guide; the top photo, scaled by the pitch, gives about 27.5 x 53 (rough): not measured on this board yet

tallest_above_board.source: estimate (the ESP-WROOM-32 can and the micro-USB socket), not measured

footprint.name: ESP32_DEVKITC_38
footprint.why: drill 1.0 mm for 0.64 mm square header pins (diagonal 0.9 mm), pad 1.7 mm: the common 2.54 mm header land; the body outline is drawn centred on the pins

pin_numbering: 1-19 down the left row and 20-38 down the right row, antenna at the top, seen from above
pins: 3.3 V out of the board's regulator
GPIO12, strapping pin: keep low at boot
GPIO9, wired to the module's flash: do not use
GPIO10, wired to the module's flash: do not use
GPIO11, wired to the module's flash: do not use
5 V from USB, or 5 V in
GPIO1, UART0 TX to the USB chip
GPIO3, UART0 RX from the USB chip
GPIO0, strapping pin: low at reset = download mode (BOOT button)
GPIO2, strapping pin; an LED on many clones
GPIO8, wired to the module's flash: do not use
GPIO7, wired to the module's flash: do not use
GPIO6, wired to the module's flash: do not use
